newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Southern Africa to discuss water, tourism.
newsitem.headline: Southern Africa to discuss water, tourism.

text.p: Southern African states will meet in the Namibian capital Windhoek next month to discuss progress on shared water resources and regional tourism.

Southern African Development Community (SADC) executive secretary Kaire Mbuende told reporters the February 9 and 10 conference of the 12 SADC member states will discuss progress in sharing water resources and moves to establish a regional tourist body.
"SADC priorities for 1997 are to ratify the protocol on shared water course systems, finalise the draft protocol on tourism and get the tourism organisation off the ground," Mbuende said.
The conference will also focus on productivity in southern Africa. "We can no longer hide low productivity and non-competitiveness behind high tariff walls," Mbuende said.
"Given the need for regional development, we have first to address national production. The message is you have to be productive to survive," he added.
Mbuende said SADC members should each establish a national productivity movement as the basis for a regional effort.
"The heads of state should declare productivity the only means by which the region can survive in the new global economic order."
SADC comprises Angola, Botswana, Lesotho, Malawi, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Swaziland, South Africa, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe.
